issues.desc: background.md ## Key Insights says "Each of the four has a concrete mutation ... deleting a policy row, squashing a RED commit, a FAIL verdict with unreadable findings, a receipt whose own outputTail contradicted its result." The first three mutations map to CHK-002/CHK-003/CHK-004, but the fourth (outputTail contradiction) is the B-a745:F-002 evidence-pin/selector defect that the same background explicitly says (Trigger Event paragraph) is handled by the separate sibling draft narrowing-only-evidence-repin, not by this story. CHK-001 (the orphan validation-protocol-smoke item) has no mutation named in Key Insights at all. This looks like a leftover artifact from narrowing the draft from five items to four (the mutation list was not swapped to describe CHK-001s own CASE_MISMATCH failure), and could mislead a reader into thinking this story also fixes the outputTail/evidence-pin defect.

checklist CHK-001 context has no explicit RED: <mutation> sentence, unlike CHK-002 (RED: remove a real RESOURCE_POLICY row...), CHK-003 (RED: squash a RED into a GREEN...), and CHK-004 (RED: a FAIL leaf with two findings...). background.md Conversational Texture promises each item ships with the mutation that previously slipped through now failing the check, but CHK-001 only describes the current defect/remediation options without stating what mutation must make the fixed, registered check fail.

background.md ## Trigger Event references implementer reports during CHK-001 and CHK-006 of B-a745 without a one-sentence gloss of what those two items covered, unlike the adjacent B-a745:F-002 / B-a745:F-012 references which each carry a parenthetical explanation. Similarly, Conversational Texture references the single-owner extraction story (draft single-owner-extraction-readers-parsers) only as a sequencing predecessor with no one-sentence description of what it covers.
